proof.criterion: AC1 - the Dispatch server accepts a comment, a comment edit, a message and a broadcast of 32,000 characters, and refuses one of 32,001 naming the limit and the count.
proof.surface: The real Dispatch Go server over HTTP against a real pgvector Postgres (CI's envoy-go job, the production-like surface the architect ruled for this pod), plus the live INFRA Dispatch server for the counting half I could reach from here.
proof.command: gh run view --repo sjawhar/legion --job 119436670878 --log (run 39661833569), read for the package lines and for the presence of packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/body_cap_test.go at the head; and, in this pod, `bun packages/envoy-client/bin/dispatch.ts comment --issue INFRA-45 --body-file <16,000 non-BMP characters = 32,000 UTF-16 units>` and the same for `message`.
proof.observed: `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/api 504.822s` at head 700a0216 with TestBodiesAreCappedOnEveryWriteRoute compiled into it - the table sends a body of exactly contracts.DispatchBodyMax on comment create, comment edit, message create and broadcast create and requires each route to return it whole. All four enforcement sites read contracts.DispatchBodyMax and no literal remains (comment_create.go:349, comment_actions.go:142, messages.go:214, broadcasts.go:217); artifact comments share createCommentFor, so the document-comment route is the same check. In this pod the live server answered a body of exactly 32,000 UTF-16 units made of 16,000 non-BMP characters with `body is 30000 characters over the 2000-character limit (32000/2000)` - it counted 32,000 units for 16,000 characters, the same UTF-16 counting the new cap uses, and it is still on the old build.
proof.negativeControl: The table's over-cap cases on every one of the four routes - DispatchBodyMax+1 ASCII units, and DispatchBodyMax/2+1 non-BMP characters that count two units each - each required to answer 400 CAP_EXCEEDED with the count wording. My own live control: the 32,000-unit non-BMP body above was refused by the server with the count 32000/2000, so the refusal path is real and counts units, not characters.

proof.criterion: AC3 - a 32,000-character comment posted on an issue reaches a subscribed agent session whole, over the message bus.
proof.surface: A real NATS server (testcontainers) with the deployed Dispatch outbox publishing into it and a subscriber connected as a listener lane would be, in CI's envoy-go job; plus a read of the whole delivery path for a second cap.
proof.command: gh run view --repo sjawhar/legion --job 119436670878 --log (run 39661833569), package github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox; and a search of the delivery path for any truncation between the outbox and a session (`grep -rn "maxEnvelopeTextRunes" packages/envoy/internal/`).
proof.observed: `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox 40.293s` at head 700a0216, with TestRunDeliversACommentBodyAtTheCapThroughNATS in that package: it publishes a comment body of exactly contracts.DispatchBodyMax units built from three-byte BMP characters (about 96 KB) and requires the body inside the delivered envelope to equal it exactly. The one other text cap in the envoy module, maxEnvelopeTextRunes = 2048 (packages/envoy/internal/contracts/normalize.go:1253-1268), applies to GitHub webhook payloads alone (payloadJSON, checkName), not to Dispatch comment or message events, so nothing cuts a Dispatch body between the outbox and a session. The plan's separately-ruled AGENT_STREAM_LIMITS.partChars cut is the dashboard's Agent view, not the delivery.
proof.negativeControl: The test's body carries HEAD:/:TAIL markers, so a cut at either end fails its byte-for-byte equality, and a body NATS refused would never arrive, failing the subscriber's 10-second wait - which is the silent drop the spec names as the one real delivery risk. I could not inject a cut myself from this pod (no Docker socket for the NATS container); what I could do instead was look for a second cap on that path and find none.

Two deploy-order facts measured here rather than argued, both already written in the PR body and packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md: the live INFRA Dispatch still enforces 2,000 (it answered a 32,000-unit body `body is 30000 characters over the 2000-character limit (32000/2000)`), and the daemon's own posts now go up to 31,956, so a daemon of this release against that server would have its over-long dispatch_message rows refused. Those rows retry rather than fail permanently (permanentRefusal in daemon/outbox.go covers dispatch_status and ready_merge alone) and they hold nothing else back: outboxInOrder orders status rows and the supervise/issue_branch pair only, and record/store.go:774 ends `Board rows are not under it: their lane runs them as they come due`. The CHANGELOG's ordering instruction is the mitigation and it is present.

The reader-tab guard was re-measured in this pod rather than taken from the implementer: isBareReferenceBody over the three full-cap bodies of repeated schemes returned false,false,true for each scheme in 5.817 ms against its unchanged 2,000 ms budget (the implementer measured 4.380 ms). Linear at sixteen times the old cap.

`--dry-run` prints a command's arguments without running the tool-input validation (a 32,001-character body and an 801-character question both print). That is how it behaves on main too and is outside this issue; every refusal recorded above was observed without it.
